corpus_character: COMPETITIVE / HISTORICAL desk research collected by the assistant via web search. NOT operator-voice community signal. The Reddit path was rate-limited to zero (see source-status.json), so no cluster below rests on a practitioner describing their own pain in their own words. Every cluster is structural or competitive evidence about the market, which is a different and weaker thing for a desirability claim.
sisp_guard_status: NOT SATISFIED. belief.md requires the design-to-machine pain to be shown independently in operators' own language before solution-shaped vocabulary is used. That test has not been run. Candidates below are proposed on competitive and structural grounds only.

clusters.label: Batch-size-one with automated quoting is a 25-year-old solved business in metal and plastic
evidence: Protolabs: customer uploads CAD, software runs manufacturability analysis and returns a firm price in minutes, then generates toolpaths; ~1M sq ft of owned facilities; 1-200 parts in 1-3 business days. https://www.amtonline.org/article/protolabs-innovation-in-low-volume-manufacturing
Xometry: CAD upload, instant quote, auto-matched to one of 5,000+ partner shops. https://www.xometry.com/
clusters.implication: The belief's why-now ('LLMs plus constraint solvers make this newly possible') is not supported for metal and plastic. The capability shipped in 1999. Any why-now claim has to explain why WOOD and PANEL never got it, not why the technology is new.

clusters.label: Owning the factory and not owning it are BOTH viable - they buy different things
evidence: Protolabs (asset-heavy) gross margin 44% vs Xometry (asset-light) 35.7%; Protolabs equal or cheaper at 1-10 parts because there is no marketplace markup; Xometry serves four continents without owning factories. https://umbrex.com/resources/company-profiles/protolabs/
Both are public companies operating today.
clusters.implication: Ownership buys unit economics at batch size one. Asset-light buys scale and geography. This does NOT falsify 'you have to own both ends' - it bounds it to low volume. But it does partially satisfy the founder's own disconfirmer #1.

clusters.label: The panel-goods version of this already exists and has for over a decade
evidence: Cutwrights (UK, founded 2009 by two cabinetmakers): cutting, edging and drilling of panels, 24/7 instant online quotes, 3-5 day lead, CNC saws to 3.8m at 0.1mm. https://www.cutwrights.com/

SendCutSend: instant automated quoting with manufacturability feedback for Baltic birch plywood and MDF on CNC routers - BUT largest instant-quote part is 30 x 44 inches. https://sendcutsend.com/materials/baltic-birch-plywood/
Cutr (Amsterdam): B2B marketplace for on-demand wood manufacturing plus SaaS - the asset-light version. https://www.cutr.com/
Perfect Panels: online panel sizes, quantities, edgebanding. https://www.perfectpanels.online/
clusters.implication: 'Go to a website and manufacture what you need' in panel goods is an operating business in the UK and NL, not a future state. SendCutSend's 30x44in instant-quote ceiling is a real gap - it is below cabinet-carcass size. Whether the US is underserved is testable and unknown.

clusters.label: In cabinets specifically, the design-to-machine coupling is largely solved and cheap
evidence: Mozaik CNC Complete: $125/month, design through cut lists, nesting and machine-ready G-code. https://www.mozaiksoftware.com/mozaik-products/mozaik-cnc
Microvellum: generates machine-ready code directly from designs, unified post-processor across CNC brands. https://www.microvellum.com/
Cabinet Vision (Hexagon): machine-specific optimized post-processors. https://www.woodshopnews.com/features/catching-up-with-cnc-software
clusters.implication: Direct hit on H1A1. A cabinet shop buys design-to-G-code for $1,500/year. The 13.5-hour design-labour figure in the prior belief was derived from the founder's own build model and has never been observed in a live shop - this cluster is a reason to doubt it.

clusters.label: Direct-to-consumer custom-sized cabinets already ship today
evidence: Barker Cabinets: custom RTA kitchen and bath cabinets ordered online, US-made, 3/4in ply cases, Blum Movento slides. https://www.barkercabinets.com/
CabinetNow: custom-sized cabinet boxes and doors, instant pricing on style selection, 1-2 weeks unfinished. https://www.cabinetnow.com/
clusters.implication: H1 claims a ten-minute firm quote is 'a difference dealers can feel'. A homeowner can already configure and price custom-sized boxes online. The differentiator has to be something other than existence.

clusters.label: Structural and miscellaneous steel estimating is still manual and expensively so
evidence: Manual takeoff for a typical mid-size structural package takes 4-8 hours; shops adopting automated takeoff drop to under 2 hours; one estimator goes from 2 bids/week to 4-5. https://www.ibeam.ai/estimate/structural-steel-estimating-software

'Manual reading is slow and easy to get wrong under a bid deadline and is definitely the main bottleneck in steel estimating.' https://dac.digital/steel-fabrication-estimating-software-a-buyers-guide-for-structural-steel-shops/
clusters.implication: This is the clearest quantified, currently-manual design-to-machine handoff found in the run - and it is not furniture. Counts against Theobald's wedge on the demand axis while leaving his materials argument intact.

clusters.label: Stone and quartz countertops - already digitised
evidence: Digital templating is standard practice; SlabSmith exports to CNC for immediate saw/sawjet programming; an experienced operator completes a standard kitchen layout in 20-45 minutes. https://www.parkindustries.com/software/slabsmith/
clusters.implication: Looked like a candidate on the per-order-manual-handoff criterion. It is not - this vertical already crossed.

clusters.label: The asset-heavy custom-manufacturing graveyard, and what actually killed each
evidence: Katerra: >$2bn raised, ~8,000 staff, bankrupt June 2021, ~$3bn destroyed. Full vertical integration meant exposure to many single points of failure at once - architecture, manufacturing and site delivery all needing to work simultaneously. https://www.failory.com/cemetery/katerra

Prefab/modular sector overall: 'has not produced a single major exit, a durable category leader, or a scalable operating model' despite billions. Four misalignments: factory economics, builder adoption and risk, construction market realities, capital structure. https://onebuild.substack.com/p/the-prefab-and-modular-graveyard
Lustron (1948-50): failed to deliver on time, could not compete with traditional housing on cost, misread family demand. https://www.tomorrow.city/lustron-homes/

Fab.com: $336M raised, $14M/month burn, pivoted into vertically integrated custom furniture (Hem) as a late move; sold for ~$15M, a 96% loss; Hem sold on to a Vitra-backed group. https://techcrunch.com/2014/10/20/fab-hem/

Protolabs, Xometry and Fictiv all hit the same wall: 'rapid manufacturing is operationally heavy, margin-constrained, and much harder to scale profitably than it looks in a pitch deck.' Ugly economics come from quoting mistakes, bad handoffs, poor supplier fit, expensive exceptions, and customers who churn once the job gets more complex. https://hardwareishard.substack.com/p/churn-the-dark-side-of-the-rapid
clusters.implication: The recurring cause of death is not the coupling being unsolved. It is operating leverage: fixed factory cost against lumpy, geographically dispersed, project-shaped demand. Katerra's specific lesson is that integrating MORE stages multiplies simultaneous failure points rather than compounding advantage.
